newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand records Oct-March fiscal, cash deficits.
newsitem.headline: Thailand records Oct-March fiscal, cash deficits.

text.p: Thailand recorded cash balance and fiscal deficits in the first six months of fiscal 1996/97 (October-September), a finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
The government enjoyed a cash balance surplus of 611.5 million baht in March against the deficit of five billion baht in February.
But the surplus only helped narrow the gap from the beginning of the financial year slightly to 44.44 billion baht from 45 billion baht in February, the official said.
The cash balance, which is the government's current account, includes non-budgetary revenue and expenditure such as remittances from state enterprises while the fiscal balance does not.
The official attributed the cash surplus in March to an increase in revenue from state-enterprises, which amounted to 3.9 billion baht.
The fiscal deficit during the first six months of 1996/97 reached 53.75 billion baht, with the deficit in March alone was 3.28 billion baht.
This was due to lower-than-expected revenue caused by a slowing of the national economy, he added.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said earlier that he expected the situation to improve in the second half of this financial year. ($1 = 26 baht)
